questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13944892/assets/e00248d1dd5cb96a5e0099acf5da41913a805dbc388715f0b542aa821a95efa5.png)

The scatterplot above shows the relationship between the number of hours $x$ a group of people spend watching TV each night and the time $y$ they sleep each night. The equation of the trend line is $y=10-1.25x.$ 

Assuming this trend continues, estimate the time a person sleeps per night if they watch TV for $6$ hours.
questions.worked_solution:
To predict the number of hours a person sleeps after watching TV for $6$ hours, we need to substitute $x=6$ into the equation of the trend line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =10-1.25x \\  & =10-1.25(6) \\  & =10-7.5 \\  & =2.5\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, according to this model, a person watching TV for $6$ hours sleeps for approximately $2.5$ hours.

Note: The point where $x=6$ is not shown on our trend line. Therefore, our result *may* be unreliable.

questions.knowledge_point: Making a Prediction by Estimating a Trend Line
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13944892/assets/9fed391b00d0159e58b2e760e0c68c5b0be656a440ae898a932bfec64469b5bb.png)

The scatter plot above shows the population of a town recorded at certain times between the years $2000$ and $2020.$
Assuming this trend continues, estimate the year in which the population will be approximately $40\,000.$

*Hint: Assume the trend is linear and that the trend line passes through the points $(2,56)$ and $(18,48).$*
questions.worked_solution:
First, using the hint, let's draw an approximate trend line for our scatter plot.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13944892/assets/5b2ab039994e7c2306cad7e30717fb136b5dfc3a028db284a0e95f49b56d580f.png)

The trend line passes through $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(2,56)$ and $({x}_{2},{y}_{2})=(18,48).$

We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form 

$$
y=mx+b.
$$

First, we find the slope $m$ of the line as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{48-56}{18-2} \\  & =\frac{-8}{16} \\  & =-0.5\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $m=-0.5$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get

$$
y=-0.5x+b.
$$

We now need to calculate the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can do this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(2,56):$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-0.5x+b \\ 56 & =-0.5(2)+b \\ 56 & =-1+b \\ 57 & =b \\ b & =57\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$
y=-0.5x+57.
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=40$ into the equation above and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-0.5x+57 \\ 40 & =-0.5x+57 \\ 0.5x+40 & =57 \\ 0.5x & =17 \\ x & =34\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, according to this model, the population will be $40\,000$ around the year $2000+34=2034.$

Note: The point where $y=40$ is not shown on our trend line. Therefore, our result *may* be unreliable.

questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13944892/assets/e3319694b1112e92602219492d51116d514a88e885431ac1ef0c8f8becb0dc18.png)

A tea shop wants to determine the relationship between the outside temperature and the number of customers they serve. The scatter plot above shows the information they collected over several days. Assuming this trend continues, estimate the number of customers the tea shop expects to serve if the outside temperature is ${36}^{∘}\,\text{C}.$

*Hint: Assume the trend is linear and that the trend line passes through the points $(15,60)$ and $(30,30).$*
questions.worked_solution:
First, using the hint, let's draw an approximate trend line for our scatter plot.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13944892/assets/7adb5dd9bfcfcea8842eebfcacc704237f010f87c8ffd695afab890801237abd.png)

The trend line passes through $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(15,60)$ and $({x}_{2},{y}_{2})=(30,30).$

We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form 

$$
y=mx+b.
$$

First, we find the slope $m$ of the line as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{30-60}{30-15} \\  & =\frac{(-30)}{15} \\  & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $m=-2$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get

$$
y=-2x+b.
$$

We now need to calculate the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can do this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(15,60):$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-2x+b \\ 60 & =-2(15)+b \\ 60 & =-30+b \\ b & =90\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$
y=-2x+90.
$$

Finally, we substitute $x=36$ into the equation above, which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-2x+90 \\  & =-2(36)+90 \\  & =-72+90 \\  & =18.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, according to this model, the tea shop expects to serve $18$ customers.

Note: The point where $x=36$ is not shown on our trend line. Therefore, our result *may* be unreliable.

y=mx+b.
$$

First, we calculate the slope $m$ of the line as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{3-9}{25-21} \\  & =\frac{(-6)}{4} \\  & =-1.5\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $m=-1.5$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get

$$
y=-1.5x+b.
$$

We now need to calculate the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can do this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(21,9):$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-1.5x+b \\ 9 & =-1.5(21)+b \\ 9 & =-31.5+b \\ b & =40.5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$
y=-1.5x+40.5.
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation above and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-1.5x+40.5 \\ 0 & =-1.5x+40.5 \\ 1.5x & =40.5 \\ x & =27\end{aligned}

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Using Trend Line Equations to Make a Prediction
canonical_examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13944892/assets/ecce4e60594a69e040328cc8f65300f7ad1ecfe20806d9be08f154fe2beb1246.png)

The scatter plot above shows the relationship between a book’s spine thickness (in millimetres) and the total number of pages for a random sample of children's books. The equation of the trend line is $y = 10x.$ Assuming this trend continues, estimate the thickness of a book with $200$ pages.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To predict the thickness in a book with $200$ pages, we need to substitute $y = 200$ into the equation of the trend line and solve for $x\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =10x \\ 200 & =10x \\ \frac{200}{10} & =x \\ 20 & =x \\ x & =20\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, according to this model, a book with $200$ pages should have approximately a thickness of $20\text{ mm}.$

**Note:** The point where $y=200$ is not shown on our trend line. Therefore, our result *may* be unreliable.

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Making a Prediction by Estimating a Trend Line
canonical_examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13944892/assets/51ecea6126e2bc887610e5a775f6cc82906c4eb1f569277bbc626d0502bd9efa.png)

The scatter plot shows the value of an artwork, in thousands of dollars, several decades after it was created. Assuming this trend continues, estimate the time it takes for the work of art to be worth $\[math]5\,000.$

*Hint: Assume the trend is linear and that the trend line passes through the points $(1,1.5)$ and $(4,3).$*
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, using the hint, let's draw an approximate trend line for our scatter plot.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13944892/assets/761a2d3608402bb18b3574040556618d5bb0fa2c9bb53ddcb382f3779ae1af0b.png)

The trend line passes through $(x_1,y_1) = (1,1.5)$ and $(x_2,y_2) = (4,3).$

We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form 

$$
y = mx + b.
$$

First, we find the slope $m$ of the line as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{3-1.5}{4-1} \\  & =\frac{1.5}{3} \\  & =0.5\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $m = 0.5$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get

$$
y = 0.5x + b.
$$

We now need to calculate the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can do this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(4,3)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =0.5x+b \\ 3 & =0.5(4)+b \\ 3 & =2+b \\ b & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$
y = 0.5x + 1.
$$

Finally, we substitute $y = 5$ into the equation above and solve for $x{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =0.5x+1 \\ 5 & =0.5x+1 \\ 0.5x & =4 \\ x & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, according to this model, the artwork will be worth $\[math]5\,000$ approximately $8$ decades after it was created.

**Note:** The point where $y=5$ is not shown on our trend line. Therefore, our result *may* be unreliable.
